pins.title: Filter it first
pins.sub: Clear water can still carry germs you can't see. Filter or treat it every time, and follow the park's water advice.

pins.title: Make it safer to drink
pins.sub: Our filter straw removes bacteria, protozoa and sediment, not viruses or chemicals.

pins.title: Are we there yet?
pins.sub: Turn the trail into a game. Printable scavenger hunts and trail bingo for ages 4 to 10, for every season.

pins.title: Snack before you chill
pins.sub: Your body burns fuel to stay warm. Eat a little and drink often, even when you are not hungry or thirsty.

pins.title: Every trail, written down
pins.sub: A printable hiking journal and trail log: where you went, how far, who came along. Instant PDF, $7.99.

pins.title: Download the map
pins.sub: Trails often have no signal. Save the map offline, carry a paper copy, and start with a full battery.

pins.title: One road stays open
items: Most roads close to cars Nov 1
Gardiner to Cooke City: open all year
pins.sub: Plan next summer's day hikes now, when the whole park opens up.

pins.title: Clip the chest strap
pins.sub: Snug the shoulder straps, then clip the chest and waist straps. The pack stays close and stops pulling you off balance.

pins.title: Regroup at every junction
pins.sub: Agree before you start: the front hiker waits at each trail junction until everyone is together. Nobody takes a wrong turn alone.
